# Panel J4 verdict, round 3

Persona: a film-loving, design-literate visitor who enjoys cinematic, game-like sites and hates gimmicks. Judged only from the 2-second clip sheets at 1440 and 1024 (4 frames per clip, scrolled at about 250 px/s with a 2 s stop at each heading) plus the static 1440 scene sheets. I could not click anything, so interaction notes are what the visuals promise, not what I verified. Text in the thumbnails is small; quoted words are as far as I could read them.

## Verdict at a glance

- Would I keep scrolling: 1440 **36 of 49 screens (73.5%)**, 1024 **37 of 54 (68.5%)**.
- Scores (0-10): keepScrolling **7.0**, tempo **6.5**, discovery **6.0**.
- The page is a strong film at the edges and a slog in the middle. The cold open, the sea journey, the film plates, Red Dead and the Great Hall all pull me on. The Work case-study stretch (about 70 s of a 4-minute run) is where I would leave: repeated text-left, photo-right templates, dense mono bullets and a long project list.
- Games are present as a mood (egg hunt, Take off, Dead Eye, satchel, Lumos) but almost every invitation is tiny. Only the Play card and the satchel/WANTED poster read as obviously touchable.

## 2. Tempo

| Part | Tempo | How it feels |
|---|---|---|
| Opening and hero (play card, broomstick flight, name) | brisk | The flight is brisk and filmic (about 10 s), then the hero sits still for 6-8 s waiting for the scroll to start. Great first beat, small dead spell at the end. |
| Act I: Pirates of the Caribbean (iris porthole, ship, contents) | medium | Scroll-driven iris onto the Black Pearl, a title card, then a short contents page. Even pace, each beat about 4 s. |
| About (A builder of quantitative systems) | slow | First wall of text: 8-12 s of small serif columns. It stops the film dead. |
| The Crossing (journey scrollytelling on the sea) | medium | Pinned plate changes with each short beat (harbour, storm, moonlit teal, sunrise); steady and the best use of scroll in the page. |
| Act II: 3 Idiots workshop opener (wave wipe, chalkboard, pen) | medium | A wave wipe into a lecture hall and a title card; a deliberate dwell on the image, then a pan. |
| Work case studies (Led by what survived scrutiny ... kill-list) | slow | About 70 s of a 4-minute run (over a quarter of the page): text-left, photo-right case studies, dense mono bullets and a long project list. Pauses and dead dark areas pile up. Chalkboard, blueprint and chart moments rescue it briefly. |
| Films index (Three films and a game: four plates) | brisk | One plate every 3-4 s, each in its own colour grade; feels like flipping through stills and is the fastest stretch. |
| Act III: Red Dead Redemption 2 (Frontier, Beyond, satchel, WANTED) | medium | Sunrise reveal, big headline, a pinned horse, then the satchel and the WANTED poster as a payoff. A few fine-print stretches in the middle. |
| Writing journal (Thinking in public, soon) | slow | Cream pages with pencil sketches; a deliberate change of pace and medium, but a lot of quiet and a 'soon' feel. |
| Voices and campfire (In their words) | slow | Atmospheric campfire with small quotes; 8 s dwell is long for small italic type. |
| Act IV: Harry Potter (Great Hall, Marauder's Map principles) | medium | Great Hall is a showpiece, the Map is gorgeous, and the principle cards then repeat one layout; slows toward the end. |
| Contact and credits (Let's talk, credits, Mischief managed) | medium | Clear closing ask, short credits, a film-style sign-off; the credits text is tiny but the end is brief. |

Overall rhythm: a brisk fast-cut film at the start and the middle (opening, the sea journey, the four film plates), then a long slow valley (Work) that is over a quarter of the runtime, then a recovering second half (Red Dead, Great Hall, Map). The page needs its slow stretches to be shorter or more varied, not removed: the image-led holds (chalkboard, sunrise, Great Hall) feel earned, the text-led holds do not.

At 1024 the pacing is the same shape but the Work stretch is a little longer in screens (16 vs 14), and the principle cards add two more screens of one repeated layout.

Read as a visitor: the page never says in plain words, at a size I would notice, that there is a game. The only sentence that does is the small hint under the contents heading. A film-lover would spot the Play card, the satchel and the WANTED poster, and might never see the egg counter or the Take off pill.

Nothing is outright broken: no overlaps that hide text, no layout collapse, no stuck frames. The problems are dwell and density (hero still, About wall, scrutiny screen, Work bullets and lists, credits) and a few semi-transparent title cards caught mid-fade.

## 5. What I would change first

1. Cut or break up the Work stretch: it is a quarter of the runtime and my yes rate there is about 40%. Replace one of the repeated text-left, photo-right case studies with a chalkboard or blueprint beat and shorten the project list.
2. Give the About wall one picture or a pinned image, or trim it to two principles; it is the first place a cinematic visitor leaves.
3. Make the game invitations bigger once: the egg counter, the Take off pill and the hint line are 7-9 px type at these widths.
4. Shorten the 6-8 s hero hold and the 8 s dwell on text-only screens (scrutiny, About, Map).
5. Keep the cold open, the iris, the sea journey, the film plates, the satchel and WANTED poster, and the Great Hall exactly as they are.
